title: Stage 1: The Deployment
summary: Run three copies of the API and check the manifest before it reaches the cluster.

steps.title: What you are building
body: Over five stages you will take `shop/api` (an ASP.NET Core API listening on 8080) and its PostgreSQL database to a production-shaped setup in namespace `shop`:
users -> Gateway -> Service shop-api -> 3..10 api pods -> Service db -> db-0 -> PVC

Each stage has you read and complete the real manifests, then write the kind of check a platform team runs in CI before anything is applied (tools such as kubeconform, kube-linter and OPA/Kyverno policies do exactly this).
metadata: { name: shop-api, namespace: shop, labels: { app: shop-api } }

steps.prompt: Complete the parts that tie the Deployment to its pods.
steps.explain: The selector must match the template's labels, or the API server rejects the Deployment: *selector does not match template labels*.

steps.prompt: Why is `image: shop/api:latest` a bad choice for this Deployment?
options: `latest` does not say which version runs, so two nodes may run different builds, and changing what `latest` points to does not trigger a rollout
Kubernetes does not support the `latest` tag
`latest` images are always pulled from Docker Hub
steps.explain: Pin a version (or better, a digest `@sha256:...`). Then the image change *is* a template change, which gives you a rollout and a rollback point.

steps.prompt: Your first `kubectl apply` used `registry.example.com/shop/api:1.4.0`, but the registry is private and no pull secret exists. After a minute, what STATUS do the pods show?

steps.title: Lint the Deployment
prompt: Model the Deployment as a record (provided by the tests, at the bottom):
record Deploy(int Replicas, Dictionary<string, string> Selector, Dictionary<string, string> TemplateLabels, string Image);
Write `List<string> Lint(Deploy d)` returning problems in this order:
1. `"selector is empty"` if the selector has no entries; otherwise `"selector does not match template labels"` if some selector pair is missing from `TemplateLabels`
3. `"image has no tag"` if the part after the last `/` has no `:` and the image has no `@`; `"image uses latest"` if the tag is `latest`
**Run checks** builds several Deployments and lints them.
solution: else if (!d.Selector.All(kv => d.TemplateLabels.TryGetValue(kv.Key, out var v) && v == kv.Value))
problems.Add("selector does not match template labels");
if (d.Replicas < 2) problems.Add("replicas should be at least 2");
template: Dojo.Eq("the stage manifest is clean", new List<string>(), Lint(new Deploy(3, dojoSel, dojoTpl, "registry.example.com/shop/api:1.4.0")));
Dojo.Eq("registry port is not a tag", new List<string> { "image has no tag" }, Lint(new Deploy(3, dojoSel, dojoTpl, "registry.example.com:5000/shop/api")));
Dojo.Eq("latest", new List<string> { "image uses latest" }, Lint(new Deploy(3, dojoSel, dojoTpl, "shop/api:latest")));
Dojo.Eq("digest is fine", new List<string>(), Lint(new Deploy(2, dojoSel, dojoTpl, "shop/api@sha256:abc123")));
Dojo.Eq("mismatch and one replica", new List<string> { "selector does not match template labels", "replicas should be at least 2" },
Dojo.Eq("empty selector", new List<string> { "selector is empty" }, Lint(new Deploy(3, new(), dojoTpl, "shop/api:1.4.0")));
record Deploy(int Replicas, Dictionary<string, string> Selector, Dictionary<string, string> TemplateLabels, string Image);
hints: For the tag, look only at the text after the last `/`: `registry:5000/shop/api` has a colon, but it belongs to the registry.
